verses.zh: 「比撒列和亚何利亚伯，并一切心里有智慧的，就是蒙耶和华赐智慧聪明、叫他知道做圣所各样使用之工的，都要照耶和华所吩咐的做工。」
verses.en: So Bezalel and Oholiab and every skilled person[NOTE:1] in whom the Lord has put skill[NOTE:2] and ability[NOTE:3] to know how[NOTE:4] to do all the work for the service[NOTE:5] of the sanctuary are to do the work[NOTE:6] according to all that the Lord has commanded.”
notes: Heb “wise of [in] heart.”
Heb “wisdom.”
Heb “understanding, discernment.”
The relative clause includes this infinitive clause that expresses either the purpose or the result of God’s giving wisdom and understanding to these folk.

This noun is usually given an interpretive translation. B. Jacob renders the bound relationship as “the holy task” or “the sacred task” (Exodus, 1019). The NIV makes it “constructing,” so read “the work of constructing the sanctuary.”

The first word of the verse is a perfect tense with vav (ו) consecutive; it is singular because it agrees with the first of the compound subject. The sentence is a little cumbersome because of the extended relative clause in the middle.

verses.zh: 凡耶和华赐他心里有智慧、而且受感前来做这工的，摩西把他们和比撒列并亚何利亚伯一同召来。
verses.en: Moses summoned[NOTE:1] Bezalel and Oholiab and every skilled person in whom[NOTE:2] the Lord had put skill—everyone whose heart stirred him[NOTE:3] to volunteer[NOTE:4] to do the work.
notes: The verb קָרָא (qaraʾ) plus the preposition “to”—“to call to” someone means “to summon” that person.
Here there is a slight change: “in whose heart Yahweh had put skill.”
Or “whose heart was willing.”
The verb means more than “approach” or “draw near”; קָרַב (qarav) is the word used for drawing near the altar as in bringing an offering. Here they offer themselves, their talents and their time.

verses.zh: 这些人就从摩西收了以色列人为做圣所并圣所使用之工所拿来的礼物。百姓每早晨还把甘心献的礼物拿来。
verses.en: They received from Moses all the offerings the Israelites had brought to do[NOTE:1] the work for the service of the sanctuary, and they still continued to bring him a freewill offering each morning.[NOTE:2]
notes: In the Hebrew text the infinitive “to do it” comes after “sanctuary”; it makes a smoother rendering in English to move it forward, rather than reading “brought for the work.”
Heb “in the morning, in the morning.”

verses.zh: 凡做圣所一切工的智慧人各都离开他所做的工，
verses.en: So all the skilled people who were doing all the work on the sanctuary came from the work[NOTE:1] they were doing
notes: Heb “a man, a man from his work”; or “each one from his work.”

verses.zh: 来对摩西说：「百姓为耶和华吩咐使用之工所拿来的，富富有余。」
verses.en: and told Moses, “The people are bringing much more than[NOTE:1] is needed for the completion[NOTE:2] of the work which the Lord commanded us to do!”[NOTE:3]
notes: The construction uses the verbal hendiadys: מַרְבִּים לְהָבִיא (marbim lehaviʾ) is the Hiphil participle followed (after the subject) by the Hiphil infinitive construct. It would read, “they multiply…to bring,” meaning, “they bring more” than is needed.
Heb “for the service” (so KJV, ASV).
The last clause is merely the infinitive with an object—“to do it.” It clearly means the skilled workers are to do it.

verses.zh: 摩西传命，他们就在全营中宣告说：「无论男女，不必再为圣所拿甚么礼物来。」这样才拦住百姓不再拿礼物来。
verses.en: Moses instructed them to take[NOTE:1] his message[NOTE:2] throughout the camp, saying, “Let no man or woman do anymore work for the offering for the sanctuary.” So the people were restrained from bringing any more.[NOTE:3]
notes: The verse simply reads, “and Moses commanded and they caused [a voice] to cross over in the camp.” The second preterite with the vav may be subordinated to the first clause, giving the intent (purpose or result).
Heb “voice.”
The verse ends with the infinitive serving as the object of the preposition: “from bringing.”

verses.zh: 因为他们所有的材料够做一切当做的物，而且有余。
verses.en: Now the materials were more than enough[NOTE:1] for them to do all the work.[NOTE:2]
notes: This part of the sentence comes from the final verb, the Hiphil infinitive—leave over, meaning, have more than enough (see BDB 451 s.v. יָתַר).

Heb “for all the work, to do it.”sn This lengthy section (35:1-36:7) forms one of the most remarkable sections in the book. Here there is a mixture of God’s preparation of people to do the work and their willingness to give and to serve. It not only provides insight into this renewed community of believers, but it also provides a timeless message for the church. The point is clear enough: In response to God’s commission, and inspired by God’s Spirit, the faithful and willing people rally to support and participate in the Lord’s work.

verses.zh: 他们中间，凡心里有智慧做工的，用十幅幔子做帐幕。这幔子是比撒列用捻的细麻和蓝色、紫色、朱红色线制造的，并用巧匠的手工绣上基路伯。
verses.en: All the skilled among those who were doing the work made the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue and purple and scarlet yarn; they were made with cherubim that were the work of an artistic designer.

verses.zh: 每幅幔子长二十八肘，宽四肘，都是一样的尺寸。
verses.en: The length of one curtain was 42 feet, and the width of one curtain was 6 feet—the same size for each of the curtains.

verses.zh: 他使这五幅幔子幅幅相连，又使那五幅幔子幅幅相连；
verses.en: He joined[NOTE:1] five of the curtains to one another, and the other[NOTE:2] five curtains he joined to one another.
notes: The verb is singular since it probably is referring to Bezalel, but since he would not do all the work himself, it may be that the verbs could be given a plural subject: “they joined.”
The words “the other” have been supplied.

verses.zh: 在这相连的幔子末幅边上做蓝色的钮扣，在那相连的幔子末幅边上也照样做；
verses.en: He made loops of blue material along the edge of the end curtain in the first set; he did the same along the edge of the end curtain in the second set.

verses.zh: 在这相连的幔子上做五十个钮扣，在那相连的幔子上也做五十个钮扣，都是两两相对；
verses.en: He made 50 loops on the first curtain, and he made 50 loops on the end curtain that was in the second set, with the loops opposite one another.

verses.zh: 又做五十个金钩，使幔子相连。这才成了一个帐幕。
verses.en: He made 50 gold clasps and joined the curtains together to one another with the clasps, so that the tabernacle was a unit.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “one.”

verses.zh: 他用山羊毛织十一幅幔子，作为帐幕以上的罩棚。
verses.en: He made curtains of goats’ hair for a tent over the tabernacle; he made 11 curtains.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “eleven curtains he made them.”

verses.zh: 每幅幔子长三十肘，宽四肘；十一幅幔子都是一样的尺寸。
verses.en: The length of one curtain was 45 feet, and the width of one curtain was 6 feet—one size for all 11 curtains.

verses.zh: 他把五幅幔子连成一幅，又把六幅幔子连成一幅；
verses.en: He joined five curtains by themselves and six curtains by themselves.

verses.zh: 在这相连的幔子末幅边上做五十个钮扣，在那相连的幔子末幅边上也做五十个钮扣；
verses.en: He made 50 loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set and 50 loops along the edge of the curtain that joined the second set.

verses.zh: 又做五十个铜钩，使罩棚连成一个；
verses.en: He made 50 bronze clasps to join the tent together so that it might be a unit.[NOTE:1]
notes: The construction uses the infinitive construct from the verb “to be” to express this purpose clause: “to be one,” or, “so that it might be a unit.”

verses.zh: 并用染红的公羊皮做罩棚的盖，再用海狗皮做一层罩棚上的顶盖。
verses.en: He made a covering for the tent out of ram skins dyed red and over that a covering of fine leather.[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on this phrase in Exod 25:5.

verses.zh: 他用皂荚木做帐幕的竖板。
verses.en: He made the frames[NOTE:1] for the tabernacle of acacia wood[NOTE:2] as uprights.[NOTE:3]
notes: There is debate whether the word הַקְּרָשִׁים (haqqerashim) means “boards” or “frames” or “planks” (see Ezek 27:6) or “beams,” given the size of them. The literature on this includes M. Haran, “The Priestly Image of the Tabernacle,” HUCA 36 (1965): 192; B. A. Levine, “The Description of the Tabernacle Texts of the Pentateuch,” JAOS 85 (1965): 307-18; J. Morgenstern, “The Ark, the Ephod, and the Tent,” HUCA 17 (1942/43): 153-265; 18 (1943/44): 1-52.
“Wood” is an adverbial accusative.
The plural participle “standing” refers to how these items will be situated; they will be vertical rather than horizontal (U. Cassuto, Exodus, 354).

verses.zh: 每块长十肘，宽一肘半；
verses.en: The length of each[NOTE:1] frame was 15 feet, the width of each[NOTE:2] frame was 2¼ feet,
notes: Heb “the frame.”
Heb “the one.”

verses.zh: 每块有两榫相对。帐幕一切的板都是这样做。
verses.en: with[NOTE:1] two projections per frame parallel one to another.[NOTE:2] He made all the frames of the tabernacle in this way.
notes: Heb “two hands to the one frame.”
Heb “joined one to one.”

verses.zh: 帐幕的南面做板二十块。
verses.en: So he made frames for the tabernacle: 20 frames for the south side.

verses.zh: 在这二十块板底下又做四十个带卯的银座：两卯接这块板上的两榫，两卯接那块板上的两榫。
verses.en: He made 40 silver bases under the 20 frames—two bases under the first frame for its two projections, and likewise[NOTE:1] two bases under the next frame for its two projections,
notes: The clause is repeated to show the distributive sense; it literally says, “and two bases under the one frame for its two projections.”

verses.zh: 帐幕的第二面，就是北面，也做板二十块
verses.en: and for the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, he made 20 frames

verses.zh: 和带卯的银座四十个：这板底下有两卯，那板底下也有两卯。
verses.en: and their 40 silver bases, two bases under the first frame and two bases under the next[NOTE:1] frame.
notes: Heb “under the one frame” again.

verses.zh: 帐幕的后面，就是西面，做板六块。
verses.en: And for the back of the tabernacle on the west he made six frames.

verses.zh: 帐幕后面的拐角做板两块。
verses.en: He made two frames for the corners of the tabernacle on the back.

verses.zh: 板的下半截是双的，上半截是整的，直到第一个环子；在帐幕的两个拐角上都是这样做。
verses.en: At the two corners[NOTE:1] they were doubled at the lower end and[NOTE:2] finished together at the top in one ring. So he did for both.
notes: This is the last phrase of the verse, moved forward for clarity.

This difficult verse uses the perfect tense at the beginning, and the second clause parallels it with יִהְיוּ (yihyu), which has to be taken here as a preterite without the consecutive vav (ו). The predicate “finished” or “completed” is the word תָּמִּים (tammim); it normally means “complete, sound, whole,” and related words describe the sacrifices as without blemish.

verses.zh: 有八块板和十六个带卯的银座，每块板底下有两卯。
verses.en: So there were eight frames and their silver bases, 16 bases, two bases under each frame.

verses.zh: 他用皂荚木做闩：为帐幕这面的板做五闩，
verses.en: He made bars of acacia wood, five for the frames on one side of the tabernacle

verses.zh: 为帐幕那面的板做五闩，又为帐幕后面的板做五闩，
verses.en: and five bars for the frames on the second side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the frames of the tabernacle for the back side on the west.

verses.zh: 使板腰间的中闩从这一头通到那一头。
verses.en: He made the middle bar to reach from end to end in the center of the frames.

verses.zh: 用金子将板包裹，又做板上的金环套闩；闩也用金子包裹。
verses.en: He overlaid the frames with gold and made their rings of gold to provide places[NOTE:1] for the bars, and he overlaid the bars with gold.
notes: Literally “houses”; i.e., places to hold the bars.

verses.zh: 他用蓝色、紫色、朱红色线，和捻的细麻织幔子，以巧匠的手工绣上基路伯。
verses.en: He made the special curtain of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen; he made[NOTE:1] it with cherubim, the work of an artistic designer.
notes: The verb is simply “he made” but as in Exod 26:31 it probably means that the cherubim were worked into the curtain with the yarn, and so embroidered on the curtain.

verses.zh: 为幔子做四根皂荚木柱子，用金包裹，柱子上有金钩，又为柱子铸了四个带卯的银座。
verses.en: He made for it four posts of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold, with gold hooks,[NOTE:1] and he cast for them four silver bases.
notes: Heb “and their hooks gold.”

verses.zh: 拿蓝色、紫色、朱红色线，和捻的细麻，用绣花的手工织帐幕的门帘；
verses.en: He made a hanging for the entrance of the tent of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer,

verses.zh: 又为帘子做五根柱子和柱子上的钩子，用金子把柱顶和柱子上的杆子包裹。柱子有五个带卯的座，是铜的。
verses.en: and its five posts and their hooks. He overlaid their tops[NOTE:1] and their bands with gold, but their five bases were bronze.[NOTE:2]
notes: The word is “their heads”; technically it would be “their capitals” (so ASV, NAB, NRSV). The bands were bands of metal surrounding these capitals just beneath them. These are not mentioned in Exod 26:37, and it sounds like the posts are to be covered with gold. But the gradation of metals is what is intended: the posts at the entrance to the Most Holy Place are all of gold; the posts at the entrance to the tent are overlaid with gold at the top; and the posts at the entrance to the courtyard are overlaid with silver at the top (S. R. Driver, Exodus, 387, citing Dillmann without reference).
For a good summary of the differences between the instruction section and the completion section, and the reasons for the changes and the omissions, see B. Jacob, Exodus, 1022-23.
